summary: 1. The August fiscal cycle is running behind from its second day. 2. MTD sits at 41,478 BCM against a 44,510.6 BCM target, -6.8%, after Jul 26 came in at 19,964 BCM against 22,255.3, a 10.3% daily miss. 3. The crusher has moved 5,781 LCM of a 124,000 LCM monthly plan, 4.7% at day 2, held back by a single 12-hour maintenance stop on Jul 26 that is the largest crusher outage in this KB's July record. 4. Survey reconciliation opened sharply negative at -41.05% MTD, a hard reversal from the July cycle's +5.17% close, with three excavators loading on heap and overspill outside the survey boundary on both opening days. 5. Fleet availability held at 89.22% daily and 91.57% MTD, but core fleet fell to 83.41%, the weakest reading in several weeks, on Wheel Loader at 57.08% and Wheel Dozer at 54.17%. 6. EX-123 is down 21 days, DR-343 16, DT-108 14 and DT-109 6, none with a revised return date.

followUps.title: Long-term-down units drop out of the availability denominator
followUps.body: The Jul 26 report tabulates EX-123, DT-108 and DT-109 at 100% availability with zero downtime hours while showing them Down with no Date Out, which is why the excavator fleet reads 97.92% on a day EX-123 was down. Fleet availability headlines describe the machines still working, not the fleet Peter actually owns.

followUps.title: The dashboard published a month that had already closed
followUps.body: The 72nd pass wrote its Jul 22-26 catch-up entirely in prose and dropped every phrasing `publish_insights.py` parses, so MTD BCM showed a 21 July figure of 565,161, Crusher MTD showed nothing at all, Survey Gap showed a single-day -53.9% instead of the -41.05% MTD, days remaining showed 3, and the fleet block was empty. The 17:14 publish went out on exactly those figures, confirmed against the payload in `gh-pages/insights.json`. All are restated now, from the same RAW files, in the established formats.

followUps.title: The August cycle runs 31 production days, not 30
followUps.body: The Aug Client Meeting Report carries 31 dated tabs from July (25) to Aug (24) and sets a 22,255.31 BCM daily target against the unchanged 645,404 BCM monthly figure. The July cycle ran 30 days. Every days-remaining and percent-of-month calculation for this cycle needs the longer denominator.

followUps.title: Compile passes need a KPI check before they finish
followUps.body: This drift was invisible for a full publish cycle because nothing errored and the articles themselves were correct and well sourced. Only the wording changed.
